confirmed_method_findings.quote: Purchased net heat MJ = delivered hot-water mass × (supply enthalpy - return enthalpy)
confirmed_method_findings.finding: The single-mass enthalpy-difference equation is stated without a verified equal supply/return mass condition. The surrounding collection requires thermal measurements but does not establish that condition. It can misstate an interface with actual steam/condensate losses or unequal returns, and then distort energy or causal allocation.
confirmed_method_findings.counterexample: Supply10kg at3MJ/kg and return8kg at0.5MJ/kg give separate-leg difference30-4=26MJ; reusing supply mass gives10*(3-0.5)=25MJ. Neither number may be called useful heat until actual leakage, other heat losses, makeup and stored-energy change are separately reconciled. The one-mass simplification hides1MJ in this example.
confirmed_method_findings.repair: Allow m*(h_s-h_r) only with measured mass equality at a common boundary/time/enthalpy datum. Otherwise independently measure each supply/return mass and enthalpy and all real other legs, losses and storage; establish useful delivery before linking provider/allocation. Align EN/ZH and regenerate projection.
